- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 50% of spike magnitude.  
- If sentiment is high (0.67–1.00) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 10–20% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model exhibits mean reversion bias; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price volatility; scale forecast by 1.2–1.5x if sentiment is neutral or positive.  
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is high, model tends to “freeze” at peak; force a 10–20% downward adjustment unless sentiment turns positive.  
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is low, model underreacts; add 5–15% to forecast if sentiment > 0.67 and price > 1.5x recent mean.
